selected_result: Cancellation-resistant formula for the normwise least-squares backward error

bibliographic_source.title: Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms, 2nd ed., Chapter 20: The Least Squares Problem, Problem 20.9

paper_locations.anchor: Problem 20.9: equation (20.21), the computationally stable alternative to the Theorem 20.5 formulae

task_clarification: Let A in R^{m x n} (m >= n), b in R^m, y != 0 in R^n, and r = b - A y.
Theorem 20.5 defines eta_F(y) := min{ ||[dA, theta*db]||_F : ||(A + dA) y - (b + db)||_2 is minimized }.
Formalize equation (20.21): eta_F(y) = min{ phi, sigma_min([A, phi*(I - r r^+)]) }, where phi = sqrt(mu) * ||r||_2 / ||y||_2.
Here r^+ is the pseudo-inverse of r and sigma_min denotes the smallest singular value.
scope_constraints: This is the alternative formula whose purpose is to avoid the catastrophic cancellation of the Theorem 20.5 expressions when lambda_* < 0.
State the hypotheses y != 0 and m >= n explicitly.
This is an exact identity for eta_F, not an inequality.
Represent eta_F by its minimization definition rather than assuming the stated formula.
